candidate.answerReason: The number of 3-point baskets can be any integer from 0 through 5, producing the six distinct totals 10 through 15.

methods.label: List totals by the number of 3-point baskets
methods.explanation:
If all five baskets were worth \(2\) points, the total would be \(5\cdot2=10\) points. Each basket worth \(3\) instead adds \(1\) point.

There can be \(0,1,2,3,4,\) or \(5\) such baskets, giving the possible totals
\[
10,11,12,13,14,15.
\]
Each total is attainable, and different numbers of 3-point baskets give different totals. There are \(\boxed{6}\) possible totals, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
methods.levelReason: Only multiplication, a one-point increase, and exhaustive listing of six cases are needed.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is listing and counting distinct possible totals. Multiplication supplies the all-2-point starting total, and a constant one-point increase generates the complete list without repetition.
